pr_title: test: Start a pod with nc instead of execing a background command
pr_body:
Signed-off-by: Mrunal Patel <mpatel@redhat.com>


**What type of PR is this?**
/kind failing-test

**What this PR does / why we need it**:
The behavior for exec'ing a backgrounded command is not specified
with CRI, so modify the test to run the command directly instead
of using exec.


**Which issue(s) this PR fixes**:

Fixes #92057 

**Special notes for your reviewer**:

**Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?**:

```release-note
None
```

issue_context.title: HostPathType Socket e2e tests hang on containerd
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


**What happened**:
Once we switched over the default runtime to containerd, the slow ci and pull jobs started timing out. The tests, which used to take 13 minutes, jumped to 30 minutes. https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92045

This increase in test time is only observed in the slow job, so I suspect the slow job is exercising some functionality that may not be exercised as frequently in the other jobs.

**What you expected to happen**:
No performance regression

**How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible)**:
Run the tests in the slow job with containerd

comments: @kubernetes/sig-node-bugs @kubernetes/sig-storage-bugs
do we know what tests were regressing?

I did some analysis in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/92045, but basically, no single test stood out in terms of increasing the time took. I suspect that all the test cases started taking a few seconds longer, and the sum of all of contributed to the increase in job time.
I was mainly eyeballing the graphs, but we probably should get the raw data and do some more detailed analysis on it
@kubernetes/sig-scalability-bugs do we have scale runs with the [slow] tests?
As an experiment, I changed the runtime back to docker in https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92056, and the slow job tests went back down to 13 minutes.
@mikebrow pointed out that https://github.com/kubernetes-sigs/cri-tools/pull/627 may be relevant

/cc karan
/cc @lorqor

@Random-Liu pointed out that cri-tools is not used in the kubelet path, so that particular issue may not be the cause. But maybe we can investigate image pulling as a first start.

FWIW, there are at least 100+ test cases running in this job that create the same container on the same node multiple times: hostpathtype, multivolume, container restart
I think I found it. All the HostPath Socket tests are consistently never completing.

https://github.com/containerd/containerd/issues/4320
something might related

The test logs don't seem to show up in the artifacts. Running it manually, I see it hung on the exec during BeforeEach():

```
STEP: Create a socket for further testing
Jun 12 14:58:53.432: INFO: ExecWithOptions {Command:[/bin/sh -c nc -lU /mnt/test/asocket &] Namespace:host-path-type-socket-9510 PodName:test-hostpath-type-7rh6v ContainerName:host-path-testing Stdin:<nil> CaptureStdout:true CaptureStderr:true PreserveWhitespace:false}
```

However when I do this manually using "kubectl exec" it is fine.

found a work around

```
diff --git test/e2e/storage/host_path_type.go test/e2e/storage/host_path_type.go
index 231f6ae2e21f..8c1a304e28c1 100644
--- test/e2e/storage/host_path_type.go
+++ test/e2e/storage/host_path_type.go
@@ -197,7 +197,7 @@ var _ = utils.SIGDescribe("HostPathType Socket [Slow]", func() {
                ginkgo.By(fmt.Sprintf("running on node %s", basePod.Spec.NodeName))
                targetSocket = path.Join(hostBaseDir, "asocket")
                ginkgo.By("Create a socket for further testing")
-               _, err := utils.PodExec(f, basePod, fmt.Sprintf("nc -lU %s &", path.Join(mountBaseDir, "asocket")))
+               _, err := utils.PodExec(f, basePod, fmt.Sprintf("nc -lU %s >/dev/null 2>&1 &", path.Join(mountBaseDir, "asocket")))
                framework.ExpectNoError(err)
        })

```

i can easily recreate the problem locally using kubetest + local-up-cluster.sh running against containerd.

```
kubetest --build=none --ginkgo-parallel=1 --deployment=local --provider=local  --test --test_args='--ginkgo.focus=HostPathType\sSocket'
```

> There are some notes on differences between how dockershim and other CRI impls handle this situation:
> https://github.com/containerd/cri/blob/master/pkg/server/container_execsync.go#L184-L195
> 
> @mikebrow have you run into this before?

Came up here:
https://github.com/containerd/cri/pull/1256

Among the callers of HandlerRunner#Run is the following from  kubeGenericRuntimeManager#startContainer :
```
		msg, handlerErr := m.runner.Run(kubeContainerID, pod, container, container.Lifecycle.PostStart)
```
We should find a proper value for the timeout.
We have a similar issue with CRI-O. I agree with @Random-Liu that we should define this clearly and meanwhile setting a timeout makes sense.
I have opened https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/92205 to fix the tests.

review_comments:
Please add a comment explaining the reason for switching to calling nc.
It would be good to leave a TODO here once the timeout discussed in #92057 is implemented.
After looking at the tests in more detail, I think this is a better solution. We can have separate tests for exec with detach when we add that feature.
this is sig-storage test. let's please have whatever new tests needed in node e2e tests and not here.
